title: Denials Handbook: Blood Glucose Testing Supply Program Codes and Appeal Levels
content:
On the Blood Glucose Testing Supply Program a denial is worked by its denial code, and the code alone decides the route. The self-pay tier has no denials or appeals.

| Code | Meaning | Route |
|---|---|---|
| CO-16 | claim lacks information | unprocessable and never appealed; cured only by a corrected claim transmitted no later than the tier's corrected-claim window, in calendar days after the denial's posting date |
| CO-50 | not medically necessary | appealable |
| CO-151 | frequency or quantity not supported | appealable only when a medical record supporting the quantity, dated on or before the date of service, is on file; otherwise not appealed and handled as a non-covered amount under the advance liability notice rules |
| CO-197 | authorization absent | appealable only when an authorization grant valid on the date of service is on file; otherwise not appealed and handled as a non-covered amount under the advance liability notice rules |
| CO-29 | timely filing expired | never appealed and never billed to the customer; Larkfield writes it off with a billing correction adjustment |
| PR-204 | not covered under the plan | becomes the customer's responsibility only under the advance liability notice rules; otherwise Larkfield absorbs it |

**First-level appeal.** A first-level appeal may be filed no later than the tier's first-level appeal window, in calendar days after the posting date of the denial it appeals, counted in calendar days from that posting date with the last day allowed.

**Upheld decisions and the second level.** An appeal decision that upholds the denial posts as a new denial whose original posting is the appeal filing. A second-level appeal may be filed only against such an upheld first-level decision, no later than the tier's second-level window, in calendar days after its posting date. Where that window is 0 there is no customer-filed second level on the tier, and on the Medicare Advantage tier the plan forwards an upheld denial to the independent review entity itself.

**One appeal per level.** One appeal is filed per level per denial; a denial already appealed at a level is not appealed again at that level. The appeal history is read from the program's billing records.

**Window, both sides (hypothetical).** With a 60-day first-level window and a denial posted on day 0, an appeal filed on day 60 is in time and one filed on day 61 is not.

**Routing examples (hypothetical)**

- A CO-197 denial where a grant valid on the date of service is on file: appealable.
- The same denial with no such grant on file: not appealed; handled as a non-covered amount.
- A CO-16 denial: never appealed; only a corrected claim within its window cures it.
